samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` promotes an unvalidated, remotely-supplied `headingLevel` into an active heading type
samples.evidence: Attack chain traced as far as it goes: `headingLevel` is deserialized from collaborative CRDT tree attributes with no validation — `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:438` does `block.headingLevel = Number(attrs.headingLevel) as Block['headingLevel']` and the backend serializer does the same at `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:409`, so a co-editor (or anything that can write the Yorkie tree) can set the attribute to `0`, `-1`, `9999`, `NaN` or `Infinity` on a `list-item`. Before this delta that value was inert on a non-heading block; after it, `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:340-342) hands it straight back as `{type:'heading', opts:{headingLevel: <attacker value>}}` and `deleteBackward`/`splitBlock` (document.ts:267-268, 304-305) write it into the block on a single Backspace/Enter by the victim, so the arbitrary level becomes live model state that re-syncs to every peer. I could not turn this into a concrete exploit: every downstream reader clamps or coerces — markdown clamps to 1–6 before `'#'.repeat` (serialize/markdown.ts:128-132), `blockStyleId` clamps (model/named-styles.ts:108), the DOCX writer emits `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` (export/docx-style-map.ts:96) but the value is always numeric after `Number()`/`parseInt`, so no XML/attribute injection, and NaN is falsy so the element is skipped. Impact is therefore limited to anomalous state/rendering rather than injection or DoS. Hardening: have `unlistedBlockType` (or the store's `setBlockType`) clamp to a valid `HeadingLevel` (1–6, integer) rather than trusting the stored attribute, and validate `headingLevel` at the two deserialization boundaries above.
